title: Alcolumbre and Vorcaro: messages reveal friendship
seoTitle: Alcolumbre and Vorcaro: messages reveal friendship
subtitle: Private conversations between the Senate president and the owner of Banco Master come to light
excerpt: Exchanged messages between Davi Alcolumbre and Daniel Vorcaro show a friendship that fuels suspicions about the lack of a CPI to investigate the case.
author: Daniele Morais
contentHtml:
The debate in Congress gained new focus after the release of messages exchanged between Davi Alcolumbre, president of the Senate, and Daniel Vorcaro, owner of Banco Master. The content of the conversations, obtained by the Federal Police and published by Folha and Veja, brought to light the personal closeness between the two and reignited discussions about the absence of a Parliamentary Inquiry Committee (CPI) to investigate the Master scandal.

Declared friendship in the messages

On February 1, 2025, the day of Alcolumbre's inauguration, Vorcaro sent congratulations to the senator, calling him a “friend” and wishing him “the best years”. The president replied with “Hey my love! Thank you so much for everything, especially for your affection and fraternal friendship! I’m your brother!!! For life!!”. Heart‑emoji exchanges and “brother” declarations were repeated throughout 2025, indicating a relationship that goes beyond mere political courtesy.

Using friendship for practical matters

The conversations reveal that Alcolumbre turned to Vorcaro to obtain information from journalists, as shown by the January 3 message when the senator asked for the source of a report. On another occasion, Vorcaro tried to contact the Senate president to discuss a negotiation involving the sale of Banco Master to BRB, but Alcolumbre said he had no information on the matter.

Institutional reaction and CPI rejection

Since the Banco Master fraud scheme became public, senators have requested the creation of a CPI to investigate the case. Alcolumbre, however, blocked all proposals, arguing that the issue could not be a priority. In May, the Senate president used procedural tricks to prevent the commission’s installation, justifying the decision as a political strategy during the election period.

Connections with other authorities

Besides Alcolumbre, the messages include references to the Chamber president, Hugo Motta, and former Communications Minister Fábio Faria. October 2023 conversations mention parties in the “Macallan” group and the presence of figures such as Minister Alexandre de Moraes, indicating a network of contacts that extends across different spheres of power.

Alcolumbre’s stance

In a press statement, Alcolumbre classified the messages as “false personal accusations”, without indicating any illegality. The senator said he would not be intimidated by attacks and would seek to hold the authors of what he called a “low‑blow attack” accountable. The official defense maintains that the conversations are unrelated to illicit acts and that the senator received no direct benefit from the interactions.

Implications for the political landscape

The case highlights how personal ties can influence institutional decisions, especially in times of political crisis. The lack of a CPI leaves doubts about the depth of the Master investigation, while the exposure of the messages fuels the perception that the Senate president protects close allies. The debate remains open, with the opposition still pressing for transparency and mechanisms that guarantee the independence of parliamentary investigations.

With information from Folha de S.Paulo, VEJA, InfoMoney.
